question: Which phoneme groups and body locations are assigned in this stage of the nyāsa?
premises: Sixteen phonemes ending with visarga are assigned in pairs.
The crown-tuft and tongue are specified locations.
The ka and ca groups are placed on the right and left upper limbs.
inference: This stage assigns sixteen phonemes up to visarga in paired placements, including the crown-tuft and tongue, and distributes the ka and ca groups across the right and left shoulders, arms, hands, fingers, and nails.
uncertainties: The exact pairwise mapping of the sixteen phonemes is compressed and partly implicit.
plain_english: In this stage, sixteen phonemes ending with visarga are placed in pairs, including on the crown-tuft and tongue, while the ka and ca groups are assigned to the right and left shoulders, arms, hands, fingers, and nails.
